title: Book Three · Chapter 10: Leo's New Window
story:
On Thursday of the second week, Ronan finds a letter at home.

Mrs Lan has put it beside the door. His name is on the front. He knows the writing.

He leaves his school bag on a chair and picks up the envelope.

Nine days ago, he sent his own letter. Now Leo's answer is here.

Mum looks up from her work.

“From Leo?”

“Yes.”

“Take it to the window. There is more light.”

He sits down and opens it carefully. There are two pages. On the first, Leo has drawn a very large shoe.

Ronan reads the words below it.

Dear Ronan,

Your pot has better shoes than mine.

He laughs. Then he starts at the next line.

I am at my aunt's house. We arrived in the evening. I was very tired. She gave me noodles, and I ate two bowls.

My room is small. I can see a shop from the window. Every morning, a man puts boxes outside. He always starts with the red one.

Ronan looks through his own window. He can see part of the yard and the blue bike.

He reads on.

The new school is not near the house. I take a bus. On the first morning, I stood near the wrong door. A woman told me to move. I nearly left my bag on the seat.

Ronan can picture Leo beside a bus door with no bag. He turns the page.

There is a boy in my class. He can run very fast. He cannot throw a ball straight. Yesterday, he hit his own lunch box. I think you would like him.

I have some homework now. My aunt wants this table for dinner. Write again. Tell me about the girl and the long track.

And leave half the bun for me.

Leo

Ronan reads the last line twice. Then he looks at the shoe again. Leo has drawn toes through a hole at the front.

Mum puts her work down.

“How is he?”

“He has a small room. He takes a bus to school. There is a boy with a bad throw.”

“Did he get your drawing?”

Ronan holds up the shoe.

Mum smiles. “He did.”

Ronan takes a clean sheet from his book. He writes the date at the top, but no other words come yet.

He wants to ask about the aunt and the red box. He wants to tell Leo about the fish. There is too much for one first sentence.

He puts the clean sheet aside and reads the letter once more.

Dad comes home later. Ronan tells him about the bus door at dinner.

“Did he get off?” Dad asks.

“Yes. With his bag.”

“Good. Both reached the right place.”

After dinner, Ronan folds the two pages along the old lines. He puts them back inside the envelope. Then he lays the letter in his drawer, above his own unfinished page.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

arrive＝到达；nearly＝差一点；straight＝笔直地；unfinished＝未完成的。

## 理解问题

1. 第一封信寄出多久后，Ronan收到了Leo的回信？
2. Leo现在住在哪里、怎样去学校？他的生活中已经多了哪些新人和事情？

## 读句子

**He puts them back inside the envelope.**

拆开看：He / puts them back / inside the envelope.

他／把它们放回去／放进信封里（them指两页信纸）。
